claim: _reservedTopLevelKeys (assurance.dart:22-27) contains exactly four entries -- 'version', 'atsign', 'enrollments', 'atsignKeys' -- and AtKeys._reservedTopLevelKeys (at_keys.dart:79-84) contains the same four. A top-level 'keys' field is therefore not reserved on either side and falls into the legacy projection, while AtKeys.fromJson drops 'keys' instead of round-tripping it. On a legacy 3.3.0 keyfile carrying a top-level 'keys' field, the first save that files typed material throws AtKeysAssuranceException('map.legacy.keys is not preserved') and the mutation is lost.
mechanism: Enumerate the reserved set at assurance.dart:22-27: 'version', 'atsign', 'enrollments', 'atsignKeys'. Note that 'atsignKeys' is a distinct field name and is NOT 'keys'; no member equals 'keys', and the file's only 'keys' string literal is at :325, inside enrollment parsing (entryJson['keys']), which is unrelated to this set. Because 'keys' is not reserved, _legacyJsonOf (:337-343) keeps it in the legacy projection of the on-disk document. at_keys.dart:759 fromJson removes 'keys' before building legacyJson, so it never reaches metadata and never comes back out of toJson. Filing typed material via addKey (at_keys.dart:200 -> _file :213 -> _containerFor :219) makes hasTypedContent (:889) true, so toJson emits 'version' and 'atsign' equal to the on-disk ones and validateMapUpdate's reserved-field asserts both pass. Execution reaches _assertLegacyPreserved (called at :297, declared :414), which sees 'keys' in existingLegacy and absent from the candidate projection, and throws.
repro: Load an at_auth 3.3.0 keyfile with a top-level 'keys' field, call addKey to file an enrollment or atSign key, then save. _assertLegacyPreserved throws on 'map.legacy.keys' and the write is lost. A bare load-and-save does not reach that check: with no typed content toJson falls back to _toLegacyJson, which emits no 'atsign', so the earlier _assertSame on 'map.atsign' throws first.
